newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Kandir sees rates falling - report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Kandir sees rates falling - report.

text.p: Brazil's real interest rates will fall to 10 percent a year in 1997 from 15 percent, Planning Minister Antonio Kandir was quoted as saying.
Kandir told O Globo newspaper he expects the average nominal interest rate to be at 1.6 percent a month early next year.
"There is room for a further drop in interest rates and it is possible that the average rate will be at 1.6 percent a month early 1997. We are on the way for it," Kandir was quoted as saying.

Early this week, the Central Bank reduced its Basic Interest Rate (TBC) to 1.82 percent a month for October from 1.88 percent in September. The TBC is a reference rate for Central Bank's rediscount lines and indicates the level of local interest rates.
According to newspapers, Kandir said the reduction in real interest rates to 10 percent a year would allow the government to save 10 billion reais in expenses with interest payments.
"We will reduce the real interest rates in five percentage points and each percentage point represents savings of two billion reais," he was quoted as saying.
